content: 1. The use of drugs that are known to prolong the QTc interval requires careful monitoring. Oxaliplatin can increase the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate through mechanisms that require further clarification. Caution is advised, and ECG changes should be monitored if therapy is initiated in patients taking QT-prolonging drugs. 2. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of oxybutynin by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Both ozanimod and erythromycin stearate can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 4. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of paliperidone via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin stearate and paliperidone prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 7. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Co-administration of palovarotene with moderate CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If unavoidable, the palovarotene dose should be reduced by 50%. 8. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of paromomycin via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Both erythromycin stearate and paroxetine prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 12. Both erythromycin stearate and pasireotide prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 13. Both erythromycin stearate and pazopanib prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of pimozide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of pioglitazone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 17. Ponatinib increases the levels of erythromycin stearate via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of posaconazole via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin stearate and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 19. Erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of pravastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of prednisolone via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of prednisone via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Pretomanid increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate through mechanisms requiring further clarification. Increased monitoring for drug-related adverse effects is recommended when pretomanid is co-administered with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. 23. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of propafenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 25. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine (antidote) by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Both erythromycin stearate and quetiapine increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. Postmarketing cases have shown QT prolongation with overdose in patients with concomitant illness or with drugs known to cause electrolyte imbalance or prolong QT. 27. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both erythromycin stearate and quinine prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Both erythromycin stearate and quizartinib increase each other's effects by prolonging the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Patients should be monitored more frequently with ECG if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 29. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Both erythromycin stearate and ranolazine prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 31. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of rifaximin via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 33. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of rilpivirine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. 34. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Avoid repeating the rimegepant dose within 48 hours if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 35. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of risperidone via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin stearate and risperidone prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 36. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ritonavir via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 37. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of rivaroxaban by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Patients with renal impairment receiving rivaroxaban with drugs that are combined P-gp and weak or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may have significant increases in exposure compared to patients with normal renal function and no inhibitor use. These increases may elevate bleeding risk; use rivaroxaban in this situation only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk. 38. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of roflumilast through mechanisms involving dual inhibition of CYP3A4 and CYP1A2, which may increase systemic exposure and result in increased adverse reactions. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 39. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of roflumilast topical by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 40. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of romidepsin via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin stearate and romidepsin prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 41. Erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of rosuvastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 43. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib topical by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of sacubitril/valsartan through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. 46. Sarecycline increases the levels of erythromycin stearate via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates that may require dosage reduction when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 47. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of seladelpar by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, particularly in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are co-administered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 49. Selpercatinib increases the toxicity of erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Consider a starting dose of 25 mg in patients treated with erythromycin. 51. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of silodosin via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 52. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of sirolimus via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Sodium bicarbonate increases the levels of erythromycin stearate through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 54. Sodium citrate/citric acid increases the levels of erythromycin stearate through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 55. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. 56. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Avoid co-administration of sonidegib with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, administer it for less than 14 days and monitor closely for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal adverse reactions. 57. Both sorafenib and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 58. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. No dosage adjustment is needed. Regularly monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function if sparsentan is co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 59. Stiripentol affects CYP3A4 metabolism and is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider reducing the dose of P-glycoprotein substrates if adverse reactions occur when administered concomitantly with stiripentol. 60. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of streptomycin via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 61. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 62. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration of sufentanil SL with any CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, thereby increasing or prolonging adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. 63. Both sulfamethoxazole and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 64. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of suvorexant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Decrease the suvorexant starting dose to 5 mg at bedtime if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 65. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 66. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of talazoparib via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Talazoparib is a P-glycoprotein substrate; co-administration with P-gp inhibitors may increase talazoparib systemic exposure. 67. Erythromycin stearate affects the metabolism of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4, which decreases the conversion of tamoxifen to N-desmethyl tamoxifen, an active metabolite with similar biological activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 68. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of tamsulosin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Dose reduction may be needed for co-administered drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. 69. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 70. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 71. Both erythromycin stearate and telavancin prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 72. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified.
